requirements.requirement: Give node1 a routed address on each of its two segments (toward node2 and toward node3)
requirements.summary: eth1 was configured 172.20.1.1/24 and eth2 172.20.2.1/24 via ifup, confirmed by ip addr output showing both addresses live and later reconfirmed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Working path between node2 and node3 (routed via node1)
requirements.summary: After static addresses/routes were configured on node2 and node3 pointing at node1 as gateway, bidirectional pings succeeded with 0% loss and ttl=63 (single hop through node1), confirming the routed path functions.

requirements.requirement: Configuration returns on its own after node1 is restarted, with node2 and node3 reaching each other again once node1 comes back up
requirements.summary: A full bounded transition is directly observed: pre-restart boot_id baseline on node1, a reboot acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot_id (fresh boot, uptime 0 min), and post-restart state showing eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls auto-restored from persisted files, plus SONiC containers healthy. node2<->node3 connectivity was re-verified with 0% packet loss after node1 came back up.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 received routed addresses on both data-plane segments, a working node2<->node3 path through node1 was demonstrated with successful pings, and node1's configuration (interface addressing, IP forwarding, and node2/node3 static routes) was shown to survive a real reboot — pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery of both addressing and end-to-end connectivity were all captured. The independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also completed cleanly for node2 and node3, each showing the same pre/post boot-identity and recovery pattern. Hygiene is high; only non-state-changing troubleshooting attempts and a trivial reboot-log artifact were found, with no unresolved residue or damaged state.
limitations: A ping check taken immediately after node1's restart (cmd-46b85bcaaf7d4b43) showed transient 33% packet loss before a follow-up check (cmd-bd28e2179e1d4b5b) succeeded with 0% loss; this is consistent with brief ARP/route re-convergence after reboot rather than a persistent failure, but it means recovery was not instantaneous.

Package-health checks on node2/node3 were unavailable (timed out) in both the before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package-state integrity could not be independently cross-checked, though no other evidence suggests package damage.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing commands chronologically. The failed 'config interface ip add' attempt (cmd-bbc34908a90a41eb) and the several failed nmcli connection-add attempts (cmd-a4ea7b0352ba4a03, cmd-9dfbb6a3acf6423f, cmd-174003e9afde491a, cmd-4eaa685cee0648d1) all errored out before creating any connection profile or altering state, so they are non-mutating discovery/troubleshooting rather than unnecessary mutations. The two successful state-changing actions on node1 (writing /etc/network/interfaces.d/datalinks and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf, then ifup) and on node2/node3 (nmcli connection add/modify/up) are each directly tied to the required routed-address and persistence outcomes and were retained deliberately as the solution. The three native reboots were required by the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. A small /tmp/reboot.log artifact appeared on node2/node3 as an incidental byproduct of the reboot command redirection — bounded, low-risk, and not indicative of abandoned work. No conflicting services, failed units, or weakened security controls were introduced; failed-services lists on node1 (system-health.service, watchdog-control.service) are pre-existing baseline conditions, not executor-caused.
